messages.author: 3455d1823a77bd5d
messages.subject: dominant markers and backcross design
parts:
Hi Karl and All
I have question on how to correctly code the genfile for R/qtl when
dominant markers are used in backcross design. In R/qtl, it uses AA=1
and AB=2 to code the genotypes in backcross experiment however AA and
AB genotype are indistinguishable when dominant markers like AFLP are
used in genotyping. Also, there is possibility to cross heterozygous F1
back to recessive parent so the progeny will only contain AB (present)
and double recessive BB (absent). We have several backcrosses, they are
all genotyped in dominant DNA markers and some cross are half-sibs
since they share one parent. I have problem to call the genfile
correctly and also let the R/qtl recognize the cross type is backcross.


Thank you so much for your help,

Charles

messages.author: ab8dbe3bec292afe
messages.subject: Re: dominant markers and backcross design
parts:
I assume that all backcross progeny were to the A strain, and so all
individuals have genotypes AA or AB. A marker for which A is
dominant would not be informative and so could be ignored.

karl
